html:
The Martu, shown on the map as Mardu from 1600 to 1815, are Aboriginal Australian peoples of the Western Desert in Western Australia, in the country of the Percival Lakes, Lake Disappointment and the Rudall River. They belong to the Western Desert cultural bloc, and Martu is a shared name for several language groups.

Their neighbours included the Yulparija and Nyangumarta to the north, the Kukatja to the east and the Ngaanyatjarra to the southeast.

The Canning Stock Route, built from 1906 to 1910, drove cattle through their country, using waterholes that Martu men were forced to show the surveyors. Many Martu came in to stations and to the government depot at Jigalong on the rabbit-proof fence. In 1931 three girls taken from Jigalong escaped from the Moore River settlement and walked back home along the fence, a story later told in the film Rabbit-Proof Fence. Some Martu families lived in the desert without contact until the 1960s. In 2002 they won native title over a vast area.
